request: Make a 90-second infographic video about sleep

claims.text: Sleep is a natural, cyclic process that restores the body and mind after a day of activity.
During sleep, the brain consolidates memories, strengthening learning and creativity for the next day.
Deep sleep stages help repair muscles, tissues, and cells, promoting physical recovery and growth.
Light sleep allows the body to transition between wakefulness and deeper restorative phases.
The circadian rhythm, driven by light exposure, signals when the body should feel alert or ready to rest.
Consistent sleep schedules improve mood, reduce stress, and enhance emotional resilience.
Poor sleep quality can weaken the immune system, making the body more susceptible to illness.
Sleep deprivation increases the risk of chronic conditions such as hypertension and diabetes.
The brain’s glymphatic system clears waste products during sleep, reducing the buildup linked to neurodegenerative diseases.
A comfortable sleep environment—cool, dark, and quiet—supports deeper, more restorative rest.
Limiting screen time before bed reduces blue light exposure, helping the body produce melatonin naturally.
Regular physical activity during the day promotes faster sleep onset and improves sleep quality at night.
Mindful breathing and relaxation techniques can ease the transition from wakefulness to sleep.
Adequate sleep supports healthy weight management by regulating hunger hormones and metabolism.
Sleep plays a crucial role in emotional regulation, helping the brain process feelings and reduce anxiety.
Prioritizing sleep is as essential as nutrition and exercise for overall well‑being and longevity.
